---
title: "Flyweight"
---

The **Flyweight** pattern shares common state among multiple objects to minimize memory usage. It separates **intrinsic state** (shared, immutable) from **extrinsic state** (unique per context) — essential when you need to create a huge number of similar objects.

## Problem

Imagine you're building a text editor that renders thousands of characters. Each character has formatting (font, size, color) and a position. The naive approach stores all data in each character object.

With 10,000 characters using the same font:

- 10,000 copies of font name string
- 10,000 copies of size value
- 10,000 copies of color string
- Massive memory waste!

### Example

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph "10,000 Character Objects"
        C1["char: 'H'<br/>font: 'Arial'<br/>size: 12<br/>color: 'black'<br/>row: 0, col: 0"]
        C2["char: 'e'<br/>font: 'Arial'<br/>size: 12<br/>color: 'black'<br/>row: 0, col: 1"]
        C3["char: 'l'<br/>font: 'Arial'<br/>size: 12<br/>color: 'black'<br/>row: 0, col: 2"]
        C4["...9,997 more..."]
    end

    style C1 fill:#fcc,stroke:#c33
    style C2 fill:#fcc,stroke:#c33
    style C3 fill:#fcc,stroke:#c33
```

**Problems with this approach:**

- Each character duplicates font data (even when identical)
- Memory grows linearly with character count
- Doesn't scale for large documents

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
class Character:
    def __init__(self, char: str, font: str, size: int, color: str, row: int, col: int):
        self.char = char
        self.font = font      # Duplicated across all characters!
        self.size = size      # Duplicated!
        self.color = color    # Duplicated!
        self.row = row
        self.col = col

    def render(self) -> None:
        print(f"'{self.char}' at ({self.row},{self.col}) "
              f"[{self.font}, {self.size}pt, {self.color}]")

# Creating 10,000 characters = 10,000 copies of "Arial", 12, "black"
characters: list[Character] = []
text = "Hello World! " * 770  # ~10,000 characters

for i, char in enumerate(text):
    characters.append(Character(char, "Arial", 12, "black", i // 80, i % 80))
```

```dart
class Character {
  final String char;
  final String font;    // Duplicated across all characters!
  final int size;       // Duplicated!
  final String color;   // Duplicated!
  final int row;
  final int col;

  Character(this.char, this.font, this.size, this.color, this.row, this.col);

  void render() {
    print("'$char' at ($row,$col) [$font, ${size}pt, $color]");
  }
}

void main() {
  // Creating 10,000 characters = 10,000 copies of font data
  final characters = <Character>[];
  final text = "Hello World! " * 770;

  for (var i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    characters.add(Character(text[i], "Arial", 12, "black", i ~/ 80, i % 80));
  }
}
```

## Solution

The Flyweight pattern solves this by:

1. Extracting **intrinsic state** (font, size, color) into a shared `CharacterStyle` flyweight
2. Using a **factory** to cache and reuse flyweight instances
3. Storing only a **reference** to the flyweight + extrinsic state (position) in each character

With 10,000 characters but only 3 unique styles → only 3 style objects in memory!

### UML Diagram

```{mermaid}
classDiagram
    class CharacterStyle {
        <<flyweight>>
        -font: String
        -size: int
        -color: String
        +render(char, row, col)
    }

    class StyleFactory {
        -cache: Map~String, CharacterStyle~
        +getStyle(font, size, color) CharacterStyle
    }

    class Character {
        -char: String
        -style: CharacterStyle
        -row: int
        -col: int
        +render()
    }

    StyleFactory --> CharacterStyle : creates/caches
    Character --> CharacterStyle : shares
```

### Refactored Code

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
# Flyweight - stores intrinsic state only
class CharacterStyle:
    def __init__(self, font: str, size: int, color: str):
        self.font = font
        self.size = size
        self.color = color

    def render(self, char: str, row: int, col: int) -> None:
        print(f"'{char}' at ({row},{col}) [{self.font}, {self.size}pt, {self.color}]")

# Flyweight Factory - caches and reuses instances
class StyleFactory:
    _cache: dict[str, CharacterStyle] = {}

    @classmethod
    def get_style(cls, font: str, size: int, color: str) -> CharacterStyle:
        key = f"{font}_{size}_{color}"
        if key not in cls._cache:
            cls._cache[key] = CharacterStyle(font, size, color)
            print(f"StyleFactory: Created new style '{key}'")
        return cls._cache[key]

    @classmethod
    def get_style_count(cls) -> int:
        return len(cls._cache)

# Context - stores extrinsic state + reference to flyweight
class Character:
    def __init__(self, char: str, style: CharacterStyle, row: int, col: int):
        self.char = char
        self.style = style  # Shared reference!
        self.row = row
        self.col = col

    def render(self) -> None:
        self.style.render(self.char, self.row, self.col)
```

#### `C#`

```csharp
// Flyweight - stores intrinsic state only
public class CharacterStyle
{
    public string Font { get; }
    public int Size { get; }
    public string Color { get; }

    public CharacterStyle(string font, int size, string color)
    {
        Font = font;
        Size = size;
        Color = color;
    }

    public void Render(char c, int row, int col)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"'{c}' at ({row},{col}) [{Font}, {Size}pt, {Color}]");
    }
}

// Flyweight Factory - caches and reuses instances
public class StyleFactory
{
    private static readonly Dictionary<string, CharacterStyle> Cache = new();

    public static CharacterStyle GetStyle(string font, int size, string color)
    {
        var key = $"{font}_{size}_{color}";
        if (!Cache.TryGetValue(key, out var style))
        {
            style = new CharacterStyle(font, size, color);
            Cache[key] = style;
            Console.WriteLine($"StyleFactory: Created new style '{key}'");
        }
        return style;
    }

    public static int StyleCount => Cache.Count;
}

// Context - stores extrinsic state + reference to flyweight
public class Character
{
    public char Char { get; }
    public CharacterStyle Style { get; }  // Shared reference!
    public int Row { get; }
    public int Col { get; }

    public Character(char c, CharacterStyle style, int row, int col)
    {
        Char = c;
        Style = style;
        Row = row;
        Col = col;
    }

    public void Render() => Style.Render(Char, Row, Col);
}
```

#### `TypeScript`

```typescript
// Flyweight - stores intrinsic state only
class CharacterStyle {
  constructor(
    public readonly font: string,
    public readonly size: number,
    public readonly color: string
  ) {}

  render(char: string, row: number, col: number): void {
    console.log(
      `'${char}' at (${row},${col}) [${this.font}, ${this.size}pt, ${this.color}]`
    );
  }
}

// Flyweight Factory - caches and reuses instances
class StyleFactory {
  private static cache = new Map<string, CharacterStyle>();

  static getStyle(font: string, size: number, color: string): CharacterStyle {
    const key = `${font}_${size}_${color}`;
    if (!this.cache.has(key)) {
      this.cache.set(key, new CharacterStyle(font, size, color));
      console.log(`StyleFactory: Created new style '${key}'`);
    }
    return this.cache.get(key)!;
  }

  static get styleCount(): number {
    return this.cache.size;
  }
}

// Context - stores extrinsic state + reference to flyweight
class Character {
  constructor(
    public readonly char: string,
    public readonly style: CharacterStyle,  // Shared reference!
    public readonly row: number,
    public readonly col: number
  ) {}

  render(): void {
    this.style.render(this.char, this.row, this.col);
  }
}
```

#### `Dart`

```dart
// Flyweight - stores intrinsic state only
class CharacterStyle {
  final String font;
  final int size;
  final String color;

  CharacterStyle(this.font, this.size, this.color);

  void render(String char, int row, int col) {
    print("'$char' at ($row,$col) [$font, ${size}pt, $color]");
  }
}

// Flyweight Factory - caches and reuses instances
class StyleFactory {
  static final Map<String, CharacterStyle> _cache = {};

  static CharacterStyle getStyle(String font, int size, String color) {
    final key = "${font}_${size}_$color";
    if (!_cache.containsKey(key)) {
      _cache[key] = CharacterStyle(font, size, color);
      print("StyleFactory: Created new style '$key'");
    }
    return _cache[key]!;
  }

  static int get styleCount => _cache.length;
}

// Context - stores extrinsic state + reference to flyweight
class Character {
  final String char;
  final CharacterStyle style;  // Shared reference!
  final int row;
  final int col;

  Character(this.char, this.style, this.row, this.col);

  void render() => style.render(char, row, col);
}
```

#### Usage

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
# Create 10,000 characters with shared styles
characters: list[Character] = []
text = "Hello World! " * 770

for i, char in enumerate(text):
    # Factory returns cached style — same object for same parameters
    style = StyleFactory.get_style("Arial", 12, "black")
    characters.append(Character(char, style, i // 80, i % 80))

print(f"\nCreated {len(characters)} characters")
print(f"Using only {StyleFactory.get_style_count()} style object(s)!")

characters[0].render()  # 'H' at (0,0) [Arial, 12pt, black]
characters[1].render()  # 'e' at (0,1) [Arial, 12pt, black]

# Verify same style object is shared
print(f"\nSame style? {characters[0].style is characters[1].style}")  # True

# Output:
# StyleFactory: Created new style 'Arial_12_black'
# Created 10010 characters
# Using only 1 style object(s)!
```

## Modern Approach

The flyweight factory is a cache that returns the same object for the same arguments. Modern languages have that built in. Python memoizes a function with `@cache`, C# has `ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd`, and Dart's compiler shares every equal `const` value automatically. You still decide what is intrinsic (shared) and what is extrinsic (per character); only the factory disappears.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Verdict: 🟡 Simplifies** — the factory class collapses into a memo cache (or the Dart compiler), but splitting intrinsic from extrinsic state is still your design work.
:::

### Feature Map

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `class CharacterStyle` with a hand-written `__init__` | `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`: immutable and hashable |
| `class StyleFactory` with a `_cache` dict and string keys | `@cache def get_style(...)`: the memo cache is the factory |
| `StyleFactory.get_style_count()` | not needed: count distinct `id()`s to prove sharing |
| `class Character` | `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`: `__slots__` keeps 10,010 objects small |

#### `C#`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `class CharacterStyle` with constructor + properties | `record CharacterStyle(string Font, int Size, string Color)` |
| `StyleFactory` with a `Dictionary`, `TryGetValue`, and a string key | `ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd` with a tuple key (thread-safe) |
| `class Character`: one heap object per character | `readonly record struct Character`: stored inline in the list |
| `ReferenceEquals` to prove sharing | unchanged: a record's `==` compares values, so it can't prove sharing |

#### `TypeScript`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `class CharacterStyle` | a frozen object literal typed `Readonly<{…}>` |
| `class StyleFactory` with a static `Map` | a module-level `Map` + `getStyle()` function (JavaScript has no value types, so the cache stays) |
| `class Character` | a plain object typed `Readonly<{…}>` + a `render()` function |

#### `Dart`

| Classic | Modern |
|---|---|
| `CharacterStyle(...)` constructor | `const CharacterStyle(...)`: equal `const` expressions are one object |
| `StyleFactory` for styles known at compile time | not needed: the compiler canonicalizes `const` values |
| `StyleFactory` for styles known only at runtime | `Map.putIfAbsent` keyed by a record `(font, size, color)` |
| `class Character` | a record typedef + an `extension` providing `render()` |

:::

**Ecosystem:** strings already get this treatment from the runtime, via Python's `sys.intern()` and .NET's `string.Intern()`. Flutter leans on Dart's `const` canonicalization the same way: `const SizedBox(height: 8)` written in a thousand places is one object.

### Modern Code

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### `Python`

```python
# Python 3.10+ — @functools.cache, @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import cache


# Flyweight → an immutable value object (intrinsic state)
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CharacterStyle:
    font: str
    size: int
    color: str

    def render(self, char: str, row: int, col: int) -> None:
        print(f"'{char}' at ({row},{col}) [{self.font}, {self.size}pt, {self.color}]")


# Flyweight factory → a memoized function: same arguments, same object
@cache
def get_style(font: str, size: int, color: str) -> CharacterStyle:
    return CharacterStyle(font, size, color)


# Context → extrinsic state + a shared reference
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Character:
    char: str
    style: CharacterStyle
    row: int
    col: int

    def render(self) -> None:
        self.style.render(self.char, self.row, self.col)


# --- Usage ---
text = "Hello World! " * 770
characters = [
    Character(char, get_style("Arial", 12, "black"), i // 80, i % 80)
    for i, char in enumerate(text)
]

# Count distinct objects by identity: the proof that all characters share one style
print(f"Created {len(characters)} characters")
print(f"Using only {len({id(c.style) for c in characters})} style object(s)!")
# Created 10010 characters
# Using only 1 style object(s)!

characters[0].render()  # 'H' at (0,0) [Arial, 12pt, black]
characters[1].render()  # 'e' at (0,1) [Arial, 12pt, black]
print(f"Same style? {characters[0].style is characters[1].style}")
# Same style? True
```

#### `C#`

```csharp
// C# 10+ / .NET 8+ — records, record structs, ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd
using System.Collections.Concurrent;

// Flyweight → a record: immutable intrinsic state in one line
public record CharacterStyle(string Font, int Size, string Color)
{
    public void Render(char c, int row, int col) =>
        Console.WriteLine($"'{c}' at ({row},{col}) [{Font}, {Size}pt, {Color}]");
}

// Flyweight factory → a thread-safe memo cache keyed by a tuple
public static class Styles
{
    private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<(string Font, int Size, string Color), CharacterStyle> Cache = new();

    public static CharacterStyle Get(string font, int size, string color) =>
        Cache.GetOrAdd((font, size, color), key => new CharacterStyle(key.Font, key.Size, key.Color));
}

// Context → a readonly record struct: stored inline in the list, no heap object per character
public readonly record struct Character(char Char, CharacterStyle Style, int Row, int Col)
{
    public void Render() => Style.Render(Char, Row, Col);
}

// --- Usage ---
var text = string.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat("Hello World! ", 770));
var characters = text
    .Select((c, i) => new Character(c, Styles.Get("Arial", 12, "black"), i / 80, i % 80))
    .ToList();

// Count distinct objects by identity: the proof that all characters share one style
// (plain Distinct() would use record value equality and report 1 even without sharing)
var styleObjects = characters.Select(c => c.Style).Distinct(ReferenceEqualityComparer.Instance).Count();
Console.WriteLine($"Created {characters.Count} characters");
Console.WriteLine($"Using only {styleObjects} style object(s)!");
// Created 10010 characters
// Using only 1 style object(s)!

characters[0].Render();  // 'H' at (0,0) [Arial, 12pt, black]
characters[1].Render();  // 'e' at (0,1) [Arial, 12pt, black]
Console.WriteLine($"Same style? {ReferenceEquals(characters[0].Style, characters[1].Style)}");
// Same style? True
```

#### `TypeScript`

```typescript
// TypeScript 5.x — readonly object types, Object.freeze, a module-level Map cache

// Flyweight → a frozen, readonly value
type CharacterStyle = Readonly<{ font: string; size: number; color: string }>;

// Context → extrinsic state + a shared reference
type Character = Readonly<{ char: string; style: CharacterStyle; row: number; col: number }>;

// Flyweight factory → a function over a Map (JavaScript has no value types, so the cache stays)
const styles = new Map<string, CharacterStyle>();

const getStyle = (font: string, size: number, color: string): CharacterStyle => {
  const key = `${font}_${size}_${color}`;
  if (!styles.has(key)) styles.set(key, Object.freeze({ font, size, color }));
  return styles.get(key)!;
};

const render = ({ char, style, row, col }: Character): void =>
  console.log(`'${char}' at (${row},${col}) [${style.font}, ${style.size}pt, ${style.color}]`);

// --- Usage ---
const text = "Hello World! ".repeat(770);
const characters: Character[] = [...text].map((char, i) => ({
  char,
  style: getStyle("Arial", 12, "black"),
  row: Math.floor(i / 80),
  col: i % 80,
}));

// Count distinct objects by identity: the proof that all characters share one style
console.log(`Created ${characters.length} characters`);
console.log(`Using only ${new Set(characters.map((c) => c.style)).size} style object(s)!`);
// Created 10010 characters
// Using only 1 style object(s)!

render(characters[0]);  // 'H' at (0,0) [Arial, 12pt, black]
render(characters[1]);  // 'e' at (0,1) [Arial, 12pt, black]
console.log(`Same style? ${characters[0].style === characters[1].style}`);
// Same style? true
```

#### `Dart`

```dart
// Dart 3.x — const constructors (canonicalized by the compiler), records, extensions

// Flyweight → a const-constructible value (intrinsic state)
class CharacterStyle {
  final String font;
  final int size;
  final String color;

  const CharacterStyle(this.font, this.size, this.color);

  void render(String char, int row, int col) =>
      print("'$char' at ($row,$col) [$font, ${size}pt, $color]");
}

// Context → extrinsic state as a record, with render() added by an extension
typedef Character = ({String char, CharacterStyle style, int row, int col});

extension on Character {
  void render() => style.render(char, row, col);
}

// --- Usage ---
void main() {
  final text = "Hello World! " * 770;

  // No factory: every equal `const` expression is the SAME object, guaranteed by the compiler.
  // (Styles known only at runtime need a cache: `styles.putIfAbsent((font, size, color), ...)`.)
  final characters = <Character>[
    for (var i = 0; i < text.length; i++)
      (char: text[i], style: const CharacterStyle("Arial", 12, "black"), row: i ~/ 80, col: i % 80),
  ];

  // Count distinct objects by identity: the proof that all characters share one style
  final styleObjects = Set<CharacterStyle>.identity()..addAll(characters.map((c) => c.style));
  print("Created ${characters.length} characters");
  print("Using only ${styleObjects.length} style object(s)!");
  // Created 10010 characters
  // Using only 1 style object(s)!

  characters[0].render();  // 'H' at (0,0) [Arial, 12pt, black]
  characters[1].render();  // 'e' at (0,1) [Arial, 12pt, black]

  // Even a separately written const expression is the same object
  print("Same style? ${identical(characters[0].style, const CharacterStyle("Arial", 12, "black"))}");
  // Same style? true
}
```

:::

### Classic or Modern?

| Prefer the built-ins when | Keep an explicit factory when |
|---|---|
| Flyweights are immutable values identified by their fields | The pool needs weak references so unused flyweights can be collected |
| A memo cache (or Dart `const`) covers the lookup | Creation must run exactly once under concurrency (`GetOrAdd` may call its factory twice) |
| You only need sharing, not pool management | You need to preload, inspect, or report on the pool |

## Summary

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" collapse="false"}
**Flyweight** shares common state among many objects by separating intrinsic (shared) state from extrinsic (unique) state, dramatically reducing memory usage.
:::

### Key Benefits

- **Memory Efficiency**: Thousands of objects can share a few flyweight instances
- **Scalability**: Memory usage grows with unique states, not object count
- **Performance**: Less memory allocation and garbage collection overhead
- **Immutability**: Flyweights are typically immutable, making them thread-safe

### When to Use

| ✅ Use When | ❌ Avoid When |
|------------|--------------|
| You need a huge number of similar objects | You have few objects or they're all unique |
| Objects contain significant duplicated state | Objects don't share significant state |
| Memory is a constraint | The complexity of separating state isn't worth it |
| Extrinsic state can be computed or passed in | Extrinsic state is expensive to compute each time |
